properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued October 19 at 3:21PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
At 321 PM AST, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm over
Hato Arriba, or near Moca, moving west-northwest at 10 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and possible funnel clouds.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Moca, Aguadilla, Aguada, Isabela, Las Marias, Anasco, Quebradillas,
Aceitunas, Caban, Hato Arriba, Luyando, San Antonio, Rafael
Hernandez, Mora and Espino.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.
properties.area: Northwest; Western Interior; Mayaguez and Vicinity

properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued October 19 at 2:54PM AST until October 19 at 4:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
SMWSJU

The National Weather Service in San Juan has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal Waters of Northwestern Puerto Rico out 10 NM...
Coastal Waters of Southwestern Puerto Rico out 10 NM...

* Until 400 PM AST.

* At 254 PM AST, A severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located across Cabo Rojo coastal waters, moving
west at 5 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to 40 knots are possible.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until this storm passes.
Wind gusts 34 knots or greater, high waves, dangerous lightning, and
heavy rain are possible with this storm.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.
properties.area: Coastal Waters OF Northwestern Puerto Rico out 10 NM; Coastal Waters OF Southwestern Puerto Rico out 10 NM

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 19 at 2:40PM AST until October 19 at 5:45PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Arecibo in Puerto Rico...
Ciales in Puerto Rico...
Florida in Puerto Rico...
Northeastern Jayuya in Puerto Rico...
Utuado in Puerto Rico...

* WHEN...Until 545 PM AST.

* IMPACTS...Rises in small streams and normally dry arroyos.
Dangerous flows over low-water crossings. Overflowing poor drainage
areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 239 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.
Between 2 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.
properties.area: Arecibo, PR; Ciales, PR; Florida, PR; Jayuya, PR; Utuado, PR

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 19 at 8:01AM AKDT until October 19 at 12:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Anchorage and Eagle River

* WHEN...Until noon AKDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris. Ponding of
water on area roadways and low-lying areas is occurring or is
imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 746 AM AKDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain across the advisory area. Between 0.2 and 0.4 inches
of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.1 to 0.3
inches are possible.
- Heavy rain will continue through late this morning. Heavy rain
may lead to ponding of water on roadways and low-lying areas. Use
caution and slow down when driving through heavy rain. Water
levels along small waterways are expected to be at or above
bankfull through Wednesday morning.


- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 19 at 9:56AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds have caused river levels on the St Johns
at Astor to rise into Moderate Flood Stage this morning. The river is
forecast to climb slowly through Moderate Flood Stage through the end
of this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.0 feet, Water approaches or may enter lowest homes
on or near Wildhog Road and nearby canals. Flooding reaches the
parking lot of the Juno Trail Apartments. Flooding on portions of
Alligator Road and Holiday Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue
Creek are flooded. Roads at Astor Landing Campground and Lake
Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood. Water enters lower homes closest
to the river on McPherson Lane.

At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on or near
Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several inches of
water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at Astor Bridge
marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged. Bartram Rd and
Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards completely submerged.
Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded in South Moon Fish Camp,
docks and yards at condominiums on Juno Trail and water breaches the
sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Monday the stage was 3.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Monday was 3.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 3.1 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1115 PM EDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 19 at 9:33AM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in southeast
Georgia...

Satilla River At Atkinson affecting Brantley County.

Additional information is available at
https://water.weather.gov/wfo/JAX

The next statement will be issued Tuesday morning at 945 AM EDT.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Satilla River at Atkinson.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, Warners Landing, Louis Landing and
secondary roads around KOA campgrounds begin to flood. At 14.0
feet, River Rock Road begins to experience flooding across the
road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:45 AM EDT Monday the stage was 14.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to crest around 14.2 feet this
afternoon, with a slow falling trend the remainder of the week.
- Flood stage is 13.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 15 at 8:39AM CDT until October 19 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in Texas...
Oklahoma...

Red River near Burkburnett affecting Wichita, Cotton, Tillman,
Jefferson and Clay Counties.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Red River near Burkburnett.

* WHEN...Until Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Near bankfull conditions extend along the
Red River near Davidson... Oklahoma downstream to areas near
Burkburnett and Taylor... Oklahoma.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 9.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 7.7 feet
Saturday evening.
- Action stage is 7.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 845 PM CDT.
